Configures which fields the HTTP access log records and where it writes them. The access log is routed separately from the main application log, so its level and format can differ. See `access_logging` for detailed field options.

| Key | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`http.access_logging.*`](#httpaccess_logging) | | |
| [`http.access_logging.level`](#level) | string | `info` |
| [`http.access_logging.log_user_agent`](#log_user_agent) | bool | `true` |
| [`http.access_logging.log_request_header`](#log_request_header) | bool | `true` |
| [`http.access_logging.log_client_ip`](#log_client_ip) | bool | `true` |
| [`http.access_logging.log_request_id`](#log_request_id) | bool | `false` |
| [`http.access_logging.log_request_body`](#log_request_body) | bool | `false` |
| [`http.access_logging.log_response_body`](#log_response_body) | bool | `false` |
| [`http.access_logging.log_response_header`](#log_response_header) | bool | `false` |
| [`http.access_logging.log_span_id`](#log_span_id) | bool | `false` |
| [`http.access_logging.log_trace_id`](#log_trace_id) | bool | `false` |
| [`http.access_logging.log_json`](#log_json) | bool | `false` |

## `http.access_logging.*`

Log-file rotation for the access log, via the embedded timberjack logger, with the same keys and meanings as logging.* above. The access log is only split into its own file once its filename is set.

## `level`

`string`, default `info`

The minimum log level for the access log, in the same form as logging.level. Requests are logged at INFO, client errors (4xx) at WARN and server errors (5xx) at ERROR, so "info" logs every request and "warn" logs only the failures.

This is what lets the access log be more verbose than the application log: the two are filtered independently, and both still reach stdout. Left empty the access log has no threshold of its own and is filtered at logging.level along with everything else — which, with the shipped logging.level of WARN, means no successful request is ever logged.

```yaml
http:
  access_logging:
    level: "info"
```

## `log_user_agent`

`bool`, default `true`

Records the request's User-Agent header.

```yaml
http:
  access_logging:
    log_user_agent: true
```

## `log_request_header`

`bool`, default `true`

Records the full request header set. Verbose, and it captures whatever the client sent.

```yaml
http:
  access_logging:
    log_request_header: true
```

## `log_client_ip`

`bool`, default `true`

Records the client address, as resolved through http.trusted_proxies.

```yaml
http:
  access_logging:
    log_client_ip: true
```

## `log_request_id`

`bool`, default `false`

Records the per-request correlation ID.

```yaml
http:
  access_logging:
    log_request_id: false
```

## `log_request_body`

`bool`, default `false`

Records the request body. Off by default and worth leaving off: request bodies on this server carry public keys and enrollment codes.

```yaml
http:
  access_logging:
    log_request_body: false
```

## `log_response_body`

`bool`, default `false`

Records the response body. Off by default and worth leaving off: response bodies carry issued certificates and enrollment tokens.

```yaml
http:
  access_logging:
    log_response_body: false
```

## `log_response_header`

`bool`, default `false`

Records the full response header set.

```yaml
http:
  access_logging:
    log_response_header: false
```

## `log_span_id`

`bool`, default `false`

Records the OpenTelemetry span ID.

```yaml
http:
  access_logging:
    log_span_id: false
```

## `log_trace_id`

`bool`, default `false`

Records the OpenTelemetry trace ID.

```yaml
http:
  access_logging:
    log_trace_id: false
```

## `log_json`

`bool`, default `false`

Writes JSON instead of text. Text is meant to be read, not parsed: the message is written as bare prose so quoted values in it are not escaped, which is not a machine-readable format. Set this wherever a log collector has to pull fields back out.

```yaml
http:
  access_logging:
    log_json: false
```
